{{Short description|French physicist (1923–1999)}}
'''Louis Michel''' ({{IPA|fr|lwi miʃɛl}}; 1923–1999) was a French mathematical physicist at the [[Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques]] (IHÉS).<ref>{{cite web
 |last=Cipra
 |first=Barry Arthur
 |author-link=Barry Arthur Cipra
 |date=8 January 1998
 |title=A Gem of a Definition
 |url=http://www.siam.org/news/news.php?id=809
 |work=[[Scientific American]]
 |access-date=2007-11-19
 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517050238/http://www.siam.org/news/news.php?id=809
 |archive-date=17 May 2011
 |url-status=dead
 }}</ref> He was born in [[Roanne]], in the [[Loire (department)|Loire]] [[Departments of France|department]] in central [[France]], on 4 May 1923, and died in [[Bures-sur-Yvette]] ([[Essonne]]), in the [[Île-de-France (region)|Île-de-France]] region, on 30 December 1999. His name is associated with [[Michel parameters]] describing the phase space distribution of leptonic decays of charged leptons, the [[Bargmann–Michel–Telegdi equation]] describing [[Spin (physics)|spin]] evolution in a [[magnetic field]],<ref>
{{cite journal |last1=Bargman |first1=V. |last2=Michel |first2=L. |last3=Telegdi |first3=V. |year=1959 |title=Precession of the Polarization of Particles Moving in a Homogeneous Electromagnetic Field |journal=[[Physical Review Letters]] |volume=2 |issue=10 |pages=435 |bibcode=1959PhRvL...2..435B |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.2.435}}</ref> and the Michel–Radicati theory for the [[Special unitary group|SU(3)]] octet,<ref>
{{cite journal |last1=Michel |first1=L. |last2=Radicati |first2=L. |year=1971 |title=Properties of the breaking of hadronic internal symmetry |journal=[[Annals of Physics]] |volume=66 |issue=2 |pages=758 |bibcode=1971AnPhy..66..758M |doi=10.1016/0003-4916(71)90079-0}}</ref><ref>
{{cite journal |last1=Michel |first1=L. |last2=Radicati |first2=L. |year=1973 |title=The geometry of the octet |url=http://archive.numdam.org/article/AIHPA_1973__18_3_185_0.pdf |journal=[[Annales de l'Institut Henri Poincaré A]] |volume=18 |pages=185 |mr=325036 |zbl=0267.22019}}</ref>

==Biography==

Michel completed his studies at the [[École Polytechnique]] in [[Paris]]. After [[World War II]], he went to [[Manchester]], [[England]], where he worked on [[weak interaction]]s. Back in France, he was teaching in [[Lille]] and [[Orsay]] before creating the ''Centre de Physique Théorique of the [[École polytechnique (France)|École Polytechnique]]'' (CPHT) in [[Palaiseau]]. In 1953 he introduced the concept of [[G parity]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Gibson |first=W. M. |url=https://www.google.fr/books/edition/Symmetry_Principles_Particle_Physics/aQc5AAAAIAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=%22G-parity%22+yang+lee+introduced+1956&pg=PA251&printsec=frontcover |title=Symmetry Principles Particle Physics |last2=Pollard |first2=B. R. |date=1976-03-11 |publisher=CUP Archive |isbn=978-0-521-20787-4 |language=en}}</ref>

In 1962, he became a permanent professor at ''Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques'' (IHÉS) in Bures-sur-Yvette, where he remained until his retirement, and as an [[emeritus professor]] until his death.

Louis Michel was President of the [[Société Française de Physique]] between 1978 and 1980, and a member of the [[French Academy of Sciences]] since 1979. In 1982, he was awarded the [[Wigner Medal]].

His scientific activities in the domain of [[theoretical physics]] encompassed many fields, from [[elementary particle]]s and high energy physics to [[Crystal|crystals]], and provided pioneering insights in [[spontaneous symmetry breaking]] in many contexts. Including a theory of [[phase transition]]s as a symmetry-breaking,<ref>
{{cite journal |last1=Michel |first1=L. |year=1953 |title=Selection rules imposed by charge conjugation |journal=[[Il Nuovo Cimento]] |volume=10 |issue=3 |pages=319–339 |bibcode=1953NCim...10..319M |doi=10.1007/BF02786202 |s2cid=122834949}}</ref> his geometric theory of [[spontaneous symmetry breaking]],<ref>
{{cite journal |last1=Michel |first1=L. |year=1971 |title=Points critiques des fonctions invariantes sur une G-variété |url=https://public.ihes.fr/LouisMichel/publications/CRAS.272_433_1971.pdf |journal=[[Comptes Rendus de l'Académie des Sciences de Paris]] |volume=272 |pages=433}}</ref><ref>
{{cite journal |last1=Michel |first1=L. |year=1980 |title=Symmetry defects and broken symmetry. Configurations Hidden Symmetry |journal=[[Reviews of Modern Physics]] |volume=52 |issue=3 |pages=618 |bibcode=1980RvMP...52..617M |doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.52.617}}</ref><ref name="six">
{{cite journal |last1=Michel |first1=L. |last2=Kim |first2=J. S. |last3=Zak |first3=J. |last4=Zhilinskii |first4=B. |year=2001 |title=Symmetry, invariants, topology |journal=[[Physics Reports]] |volume=341 |issue=1–6 |pages=7–9 |bibcode=2001PhR...341....7M |doi=10.1016/S0370-1573(00)00087-9}}</ref> and to several results in [[crystallography]].<ref name="six" />

He supervised [[Claude Bouchiat]] on the first calculations on the influence of [[hadron]] pairs on the anomalous magnetic moment of the [[muon]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2008|title=CV Claude Bouchiat|url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/pdf/membre/BouchiatC_bio1008.pdf|access-date=24 July 2021|website=Académie de Sciences}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Bouchiat|first1=Claude|last2=Michel|first2=Louis|date=1961|title=La résonance dans la diffusion méson π— méson π et le moment magnétique anormal du méson μ|url=https://www.edpsciences.org/10.1051/jphysrad:01961002202012101|journal=Journal de Physique et le Radium|volume=22|issue=2|pages=121|doi=10.1051/jphysrad:01961002202012101|issn=0368-3842}}</ref>

In 2000, in honor of his memory, the IHÉS created the ''chaire Louis Michel de physique théorique'', an academic chair for distinguished long-term visitors.<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://smf4.emath.fr/en/Publications/Gazette/2018/156/smf_gazette_156_23-28.pdf |title = Les Publications &#124; Société Mathématique de France}}</ref>
